entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Grupo Televisa, founded in its current form through the 1991 merger of four Mexican television networks and headquartered in Mexico City, is Latin America's largest media company and one of the world's largest Spanish-language content producers — controlling approximately 70% of Mexico's television market at its peak, producing major telenovelas (soap operas) that have been broadcast across Latin America and to Spanish-language audiences in the United States, and exercising media influence over Mexican political life that has been both enabling and distorting of Mexican democracy.

Televisa's origins trace to the early history of Mexican commercial television in the 1950s, with Emilio Azcárraga Milmo ('El Tigre') building it into a near-monopoly with explicit partnership with the ruling PRI (Institutional Revolutionary Party). This relationship was symbiotic: Televisa gave the PRI highly favorable media coverage for decades, and the PRI gave Televisa protected market position and regulatory advantages. The relationship was so explicit that Azcárraga Milmo famously declared 'I am a soldier of the PRI' in 1994.

Televisa's telenovela production (over 10,000 hours of Spanish-language content annually at peak) has been Mexico's most significant cultural export — Televisa productions have been broadcast in 79+ countries and helped standardize Spanish across Latin America while also representing Mexican cultural values worldwide. Televisa's 2021 merger with Univision (the largest Spanish-language US broadcaster) creating TelevisaUnivision is one of the largest Spanish-language media transactions in history, reflecting the enormous commercial potential of the Hispanic US market.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Grupo Televisa — the PRI's media partner in Mexico's soft-authoritarian period, Latin America's largest media company, producer of telenovelas watched in 79+ countries, and creator of TelevisaUnivision targeting 60+ million US Hispanics — is the most consequential media institution in the Spanish-speaking world.
